# Notes on Cairn Mechanics

## Pulses
A pulse makes a cairn grow. The growth amount depends on two things:
- A fixed stride value
- How tall the cairn already is

When you pulse, you add the stride plus a bonus equal to how many complete stride-lengths fit into the current height. For example, with a stride of 5 and height of 23, you'd add 5 + floor(23/5) = 5 + 4 = 9 marks.

## Repeated Pulses
Each pulse produces a different growth amount because the height changes after each one. You can't use a shortcut—you must recalculate the stride bonus for every single pulse based on the new height.

## Leaks
A leak is a proportional loss: you lose one mark for every L marks in the height right after pulsing. So a leak of 7 applied to a pulsed height of 50 removes floor(50/7) = 7 marks. Leaks must be calculated after each pulse before moving to the next one.

## Drains
A drain is a fixed loss—the same amount every cycle, regardless of height. Since each pulse adds a different amount as the cairn shrinks, eventually the drain outpaces the pulse growth and the cairn empties.

## Merging
Combining two cairns uses shares (fractions in tenths) and a tether (an adjustment number). You take the floor of each cairn's share contribution, add them together, then add the tether.

## Working Backwards
You can reverse engineer a starting height by undoing pulses one at a time. You solve for what height would produce the observed result after pulsing, then repeat for earlier cycles.
